data.title: Japan: 1,800 people pull 360-tonne Hirosaki Castle keep by hand
data.description: About 1,800 people came together in northern Japan to pull a 360-tonne castle keep by hand. The Hirosaki Castle keep was moved in 2015 so its earthquake-damaged stone wall could undergo repairs. Now, using hikiya, a technique that places buildings on rollers so they can be moved without dismantling them, the keep is being brought closer to its original position. Those taking part were selected through a lottery system. Moving efforts will continue until the end of August.

data.title: US economic D-Day sanctions: 'Repeated bombing attacks across Iran failed to change the calculus'
data.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome Imran Bayoumi, Deputy Director & Resident Fellow at the Atlantic Council. He sees the Trump administration’s new sanctions strategy toward Iran as an attempt to seek economic leverage where military force has so far failed to produce any results. But its effectiveness rests on several unresolved assumptions. Chief among them is whether Washington can compel China, Iran’s largest oil customer, to comply despite Beijing’s growing economic resilience. Iran, meanwhile, has decades of experience curtailing sanctions and is again threatening regional escalation.

data.title: Dolly Parton’s peerless career turned country music cliches inside out | Alexis Petridis
data.description: Beneath the wig and rhinestones, Parton was the genius behind strings of classic songs from Jolene to I Will Always Love You that continue to inspire new artists Dolly Parton, US country star, actor and philanthropist, dies aged 80 Dolly Parton dies aged 80 – latest updates Dolly Parton’s family say goodbye to their aunt, sister, grandmother - video Share your tributes and memories of Dolly Parton In December 1977, Dolly Parton submitted to an interview with ABC Television’s Barbara Walters, much against her friends’ advice. Walters was not noted for her deep love and understanding of country music. She was a notoriously tough cookie, a Boston-born, Sarah Lawrence-educated journalist who had battled scarcely believable sexism to become the first female co-host of an American news programme. The month before she met Parton, she had interviewed Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin while they were working out the terms of the Egypt-Israel peace treaty. It was all a very long way from Parton’s world, and the interview has something of the anthropological exercise about it. Walters looks aghast as Parton shows her around her tour bus, her collection of wigs and her “hand-washable and wrinkle-free” stage outfits (“you really like this? To me, it seems like horror”), and sits impassively as Parton sings Coat of Many Colours to her: an impressive feat, given the song’s saga of rural poverty and homespun wisdom is the mother of all tearjerkers from an artist never averse to yanking at her audience’s heartstrings. She asks Parton if people from “where I come from” would call her a hillbilly; regards the singer’s outfit with a jaundiced eye and tells her “you don’t have to look like this”. And, most infamously, she enquires: “Do you ever feel that you’re a joke?” Continue reading...

data.title: In Poland, compassion for Ukrainians has turned to contempt. The consequences could be dramatic | Mateusz Mazzini
data.description: Warsaw failed to anticipate that refugees would build new lives and Kyiv would demand an equal place at the European table One of the unintended consequences of Russia’s full-scale war against Ukraine was that it gave Poland a rare slice of geopolitical stardom. When Russian tanks started their ultimately unsuccessful cavalcade towards the Ukrainian capital, ordinary Poles rushed to help millions of people fleeing the looming conflict. As Polish people opened their doors to civilians running from Russian bombs, even the then ruling populist Law and Justice party had to follow suit. It seemed that Poland and Ukraine were bound for an iron-clad alliance, unprecedented in their shared history. Poland advocated for the Ukrainian cause in the west , with some success. Ukrainian leaders, in turn, praised Poles for their generosity and the government in Warsaw for contributing weapons and money to the war effort. Given that recent history between the two countries had been marked by accusations of second world war-era genocide, border shifts and postwar displacements of millions of people, it was a remarkable change. Mateusz Mazzini is a Warsaw-based journalist writing on global affairs for Poland’s Gazeta Wyborcza and Polityka Continue reading...

data.title: Iran faces strait of Hormuz paradox as strategic value of chokehold erodes
data.description: Internal calls to end war get louder as Gulf neighbours plan alternative pipelines to cut reliance on waterway Is the strait of Hormuz, recently cited by the office of the Iranian supreme leader as “the pillar of Iran’s new security order”, and as transformative as possessing a nuclear weapon, in reality becoming a fast-diminishing asset, leaving Iran increasingly vulnerable to the new planned US wave of economic sanctions? It is the key debate that is raging inside Iran, with many different conclusions being drawn for Tehran’s negotiating strategy. Those who warn the strait’s value as a chokehold on the world economy will erode, leaving the country without foreign exchange reserves, argue that Iran’s negotiators should seek a deal soon. data.title: The Dog Stars review – Ridley Scott’s lethargic postapocalyptic drama is a misfire
data.description: An adaptation of Peter Heller’s 2012 novel never finds its footing with overly familiar survival beats and a glum lack of energy Looking towards the end of an August movie dumping ground littered with more unwanted trash than usual, there seemed to be a faint glimmer of hope, a shiny treasure poking out through the dusty mass of unnecessary sequels and sex purge romcoms . Somehow, there was a $110m-budget adaptation of an acclaimed novel directed by Ridley Scott, led by a recently Oscar-nominated rising star with support from two Oscar-nominated actors and an Oscar-winner. But why then would such a film be unveiled in between the summer blockbuster season and the upcoming deluge of prestige fall festival big hitters? A cursed weekend that’s recently been home to Jay Roach’s heinous War of the Roses remake, Dennis Quaid’s Ronald Reagan biopic and George Miller’s hard-to-define and even harder-to-love flop Three Thousand Years of Longing. Ever since The Dog Stars, based on Peter Heller’s 2012 novel, had been yanked from its far more encouraging date at the end of March, there were multiple red flags flying and the rotten end of August has ultimately become an appropriate punishment for a limp and lethargic film that only briefly fascinates in pushing us to wonder what anyone was really hoping this would end up being. It’s yet another grubby postapocalyptic survival tale, an overcrowded subgenre that hasn’t just reached maximum capacity on the big screen but on the small one too. In a world of seven Walking Dead shows, the beats are now far too familiar – artfully dishevelled actors grieve for the past and fear for the future as they scramble to find and protect resources – and there’s nothing new or notable here to conjure anything but deja vu. Continue reading...

data.title: US halts all immigrant visa applications amid tightening restrictions
data.description: Move by state department to limit access is part of Trump’s crackdown on both lawful and undocumented immigration All US immigrant visa applications have been paused by the Trump administration as the state department moves to tighten restrictions and limit access to applicants who they deem could end up relying on US assistance, a state department official confirmed Tuesday. The agency launched the initiative at all embassies and consulates in early August, according to the official and visa appointments had to be adjusted to accommodate “in-depth training”, according to the official. The state department has been working on updated guidance and training since early this year, “to ensure all consular officers are fully equipped to evaluate every visa applicant comprehensively and consistently”, they added. Continue reading...

data.title: Ukraine war briefing: Small batch of Patriots arrives as Zelenskyy pleads for more
data.description: President won’t name supplier and has previously said he ‘does some things I can’t even share’ to obtain vital air defence missiles. What we know on day 1,644 Ukraine has ⁠recently received a ⁠small number ⁠of US-made ​Patriot interceptors capable ⁠of shooting down Russian ballistic missiles, Volodymyr ​Zelenskyy ‌said . He did not ​say how ​many ​had arrived, ​or ‌who ​had ​supplied them. Kyiv also ‌got confirmation of future supplies of the French Crotale surface-to-air ‌missile system, the president ​was quoted as saying by broadcaster ⁠Suspilne. Zelenskyy said this month that Ukraine needs 5% of US Patriot production to meet its needs but has only been receiving 1%. “From 1% to 5%, I have some months and millions [of] phone calls and anything else. I do some things which I can’t even share. It doesn’t mean that it’s out of the law. But I can’t speak about it.” Russia is set to extend its diesel export ban ⁠through September as fuel shortages persist in the domestic market, with ⁠refineries still ⁠idle following ​repeated Ukrainian drone attacks, three industry sources told Reuters. Russia ​introduced the diesel export ban on 8 July. One of the sources said extending ⁠the ban until the end of the year is also under discussion. Russia’s energy ministry ⁠did not respond to a Reuters request to comment. For non-diesel fuels the ban extends to 31 January next year, including a ban for export of motor gasoline . Export of jet fuel is banned, for the moment, until the end of November 2026. To make matters worse for the Kremlin, Ukraine’s ⁠military struck Russia’s Afipsky oil ⁠refinery ⁠in ​the Krasnodar region ⁠overnight on Tuesday, causing a ⁠fire, the ​Ukrainian ‌general ‌staff said. The general staff also said ‌that two gas separation ​units at the Astrakhan gas ⁠processing plant in ​the Astrakhan ​region ​were hit ​in ‌an attack ​overnight ​on Monday. Bradley Townsend, a 33-year-old fisher from Barnsley, South Yorkshire is believed to be the first British citizen to die fighting for Russia in its war against Ukraine, writes Raphael Boyd . He is believed to have been killed by a remote-controlled first-person-view drone near Lyman, a city in Donetsk, as long ago as 10 June. Tom Tugendhat, the former Conservative MP and security minister and ex-serviceman, expressed sympathies to thee family but added Townsend had been “unbelievably stupid” and “extremely misguided”. “No question about it, it’s criminal because you’re engaging in an army that is committing the most barbarous war crimes that the world has seen in decades.” German investigators found a third drone and suspected military explosives thought to be connected to an attempted attack on Leipzig airport , local media reported. The drone was discovered in Kabelsketal, just to the west of the airport, along with about 50g (1.8oz) of a suspected military explosive on 14 August, 10 days after the unsuccessful sabotage, Kate Connolly reports . Leipzig airport is a cargo and military logistics hub used by Nato and Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines for transporting military supplies. Sweden’s military meanwhile is moving to seize Russian-owned land near the Musko naval base in Stockholm’s archipelago. “The development of Russian drone warfare has changed the threat landscape for Sweden,” the armed forces said. “There is therefore a need to take measures to protect Sweden against the threat posed by both aerial and sea-going drones.” Ukraine appears to be slowly losing the war against Russia, its ousted defence minister, Mykhailo Fedorov, has told Reuters. Ukraine’s presidential office said in response that Fedorov had been positive about the conduct of the war when in office and the only thing that had changed was his personal status . Fedorov said Ukraine still had “every chance” to win but urgently needed a plan in the next few months to ⁠end the war. data.title: ‘We met Princess Margaret and she was paralytic!’ My wild life onboard the Adam and the Ants Antmania rollercoaster
data.description: With their twangy sound, madcap outfits, lusty yodelling and pirouetting pirate frontman, the band became global superstars almost overnight. But, as their guitarist Marco Pirroni recalls, the thrill ride soon hit the buffers ‘The essence of pop is, one, brilliant fucking songs – and the rest is sex, subversion, style and humour. And that was us .” So Adam Ant told me in 1995, describing the reconstructed Adam and the Ants, which formed in early 1980 with the arrival of guitarist/songwriter Marco Pirroni, who was sitting next to him. “We’re responsible for bringing back dressing up, going mad and screaming your head off.” “That’s it!” grins Pirroni when I remind him of this, as we sit in the shabby-chic lounge of London’s 21Soho venue. Back then, I didn’t tell them I was 15 in 1980, forever sprinting across dancefloors pretending to be Adam Ant, chiffon scarves tied to knees, limbs flailing like a whirling Cossack. Pirroni hears this today and laughs. “That’s what it’s all about,” he hoots. “When I was 13, watching Bowie, Roxy, T Rex, you just go, ‘I wanna do that.’ It’s exciting, sexy, about looking good, Top of the Pops. I can’t imagine anyone saying, ‘Wow, I desperately want to be in Cabaret Voltaire. They must be earning no money, look boring and nobody likes them – that’s the band for me!’” Continue reading...

data.title: The row over Rutland: can England’s smallest county survive?
data.description: Its council is due to merge with Leicestershire’s in 2028, and some locals are incensed. Can the county hold on to its ceremonial status – and biggest selling point? Mysterious disappearances have been taking place lately in Rutland, an East Midlands pocket between Leicestershire, Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire that is often considered to be England’s smallest county . Usually, there are road signs when driving into a new county welcoming you over the border. But in recent months, these have been going missing. After 10 signs vanished, the council decided to remove the remaining 17. Now there are no official “Rutland” signs at all. The area’s MP, the Conservative Alicia Kearns, is “not sure” what the motivation behind the thefts is. But they are certainly a fitting metaphor for Rutland’s disappearing status: its council is due to merge with Leicestershire county council in spring 2028. Continue reading...

data.title: Jess Fuchs: Feral review – a debut with tremendous oomph from a future comedy star
data.description: Pleasance Courtyard, Edinburgh This motormouth Australian comic fires off tart remarks and home truths then explains why she over-identifies with the Titanic ‘No hugging, no learning” was the writers’ rule on Seinfeld. Jess Fuchs decrees a similar stricture for Feral, in which she will learn nothing about herself whatsoever. “Really, I’m just here to talk shit.” That might get proceedings off to an underwhelming start, save that the Aussie’s cynical shtick is delivered with tremendous oomph: a bracing celebration of unsentimentality from an act who tells it straight about her body, her single life and a trip to Ireland, where she finds her soulmate in the form of a long-sunk ship. It’s one of those debuts that announces a fully formed standup, a cert to be in for the long haul. Cocooned in black feathers, Fuchs is an effervescing chatterbox of a comic, firing off tart remarks, home truths and off-colour comments in every direction. Arrogant yet quick to laugh at herself, the audience love her, as she pursues a Bridgerton-inspired breast enlargement, expounds on “pretty privilege” and writhes in horror at the thought of dating a 45-year-old man (she’s 32). Her mum and sister play entertaining offstage roles, and there’s a wickedly unexpected joke about the relative merits, when dating, of seeking consent versus reading the room. Continue reading...

data.title: We asked our climate reporters to highlight one idea for positive change. We got a chronicle of global transformation
data.description: There are countless initiatives around the world that can inspire people and spur them into action. Amid the devastation of the climate crisis, our journalists strive to highlight these stories of hope Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support The news is very often about the bad things (especially if you’re on the Guardian’s environment desk). Wildfires, floods, tipping points, billionaires making huge profits and buying themselves island refuges for the apocalypse … And yet, ticking along beside that is the steady pulse of what the rest of humanity is doing in response to the climate crisis. From housing developments with no cars to buildings made out of hemp, all over the planet people are ploughing ahead and changing their neighbourhoods and cities and the world. But as news stories typically need to be about new developments or things people didn’t previously know about, it can be hard to cover all those brilliant initiatives being undertaken in the background – no matter how cheering they are. Which is why, back in 2023, we decided to ignore the usual rules about what constitutes “news” and start writing about them anyway. Readers, we knew, would like to hear about them. Climate campaign 2026: help us reach 30,000 acts of support Continue reading...

data.title: Three years after his death, the Met goes after Mohamed Al Fayed. As for his enablers – well, you can’t rush things, can you? | Marina Hyde
data.description: The crimes he stands accused of required whole armies of facilitators. Don’t the victims deserve to see them face justice too? How reassuring to learn that police investigating claims of sexual assault against Mohamed Al Fayed have handed a file to the Crown Prosecution Service, a mere three years after the former Harrods owner’s death at the age of 94, and just decades after the first survivors made reports of abuse. The CPS has said it won’t provide a timescale for any decision, to which we might remark: no shit. With this case, the one thing you could never accuse any of the authorities of is being bound by anything approaching a timescale. The story does, however, certainly have scale. So far, more than 400 allegations including rape, sexual assault, sexual exploitation and human trafficking have been made against Al Fayed by at least 156 women – abuse he got away with, having died without any charges ever being brought against him. The claims span the years 1977 to 2014 . At least 21 women came forward while he was alive, and there have been extraordinary rundowns in news articles and documentaries about all the alleged enablers of his wicked behaviour, from lawyers to mouthpieces to security henchmen to the doctors who carried out “purity examinations” on his young female PAs. Continue reading...

data.title: Sex sells and wins votes – and the Democrats know it | Arwa Mahdawi
data.description: Wonder why they’re posting flirty photos and wearing tight T-shirts? It’s a thirst trap strategy in motion Despite being a card-carrying member of the International Order of Confirmed Homosexuals, I have spent quite a lot of time lately thinking about Abdul El-Sayed’s biceps. I mean, have you seen them? The progressive Michigan senate nominee is jacked and he knows it. He almost always wears a tight black T-shirt to show off his muscles and incorporates a lot of fitness content in his campaign. I’m not the only one who has noticed El-Sayed’s prominent muscles. They have had a lot of coverage, and are seen as part of a wider attempt to rebrand the Democratic party. Which, I don’t need to tell you, has a serious image problem; a poll in March found that the party is looked on even less favourably than the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency. So, to make it look less like a party that is full of out-of-touch technocrats who sound as if they are reading from a 500-page PowerPoint presentation every time they try to explain anything, Democrats seem to be trying to up the sex appeal. data.title: As a doctor, I say this: before we even consider assisted dying, fix how we care for the most vulnerable | Zubir Ahmed
data.description: A person’s wish to die can be shaped by whether they have access to proper palliative care – and in England and Wales, too many do not Zubir Ahmed is a transplant surgeon and former Labour minister As a doctor, I have spent much of my professional life caring for people at some of the most vulnerable moments they will ever face. I have seen the anxiety that surrounds the prospect of dying, and the desperate wish of patients and families to avoid unnecessary suffering. Naturally, we all want people facing the end of life to be treated with kindness and respect. But when considering the debate on assisted dying, true compassion demands that we ask a more fundamental question. data.title: The Guardian view on the French left: division makes Marine Le Pen’s path to the Élysée more straightforward | Editorial
data.description: Two years ago, progressive parties allied to see off the far right in a parliamentary election. Ahead of a seismic presidential election, that unity is missing In the summer of 2024, as polls suggested that Marine Le Pen’s far-right Rassemblement National party would win a snap legislative election rashly called by Emmanuel Macron, the perennially fragmented French left united to spectacular effect. The New Popular Front, whose name evoked Léon Blum’s anti-fascist alliance in the 1930s, came first in a poll that delivered a hung parliament. Eight months before a presidential contest in which Ms Le Pen is the clear frontrunner, the prospect of a repeat performance appears close to zero. Jean-Luc Mélenchon, the leader of the hard-left France Unbowed, and Olivier Faure, the leader of the Socialist party (PS), have both ruled out the idea of backing a single candidate. Efforts by the Greens to broker talks between progressive parties have fallen on deaf ears. Do you have an opinion on the issues raised in this article? data.title: The Guardian view on Trump’s economic threats: bullies can overplay their hand | Editorial
data.description: Tariffs on Canada, threats against Iran’s partners and bond market intervention show a president weaponising US power while making Americans poorer at home Three moves in the last week have exposed the limits of Donald Trump’s economic bullying . The US slapped 50% tariffs on another $20bn of Canadian goods – then threatened the same rate on the cars, trucks, parts and steel that America Inc depends on. On Monday, the Treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, menaced Iran’s trading partners with exclusion from the US financial network, hoping that coercion can deliver what months of war have not. And as the costs of war, tariffs and pro-billionaire tax cuts helped send US bond yields higher, the Treasury stepped in to tame long-term rates. These are not contradictory policies but a gamble: that US economic power can be repeatedly weaponised without reducing others’ willingness to depend on it. The Trump administration’s “D-day” sanctions are potentially the most consequential because they expose the scaffolding of American financial power. While markets shrugged off the immediate threat , that calculation might change were the US to target a major Chinese refinery or bank. Such an escalation could spark a trade war with Beijing. The US has leverage. But China has pressure points – especially farmers in Republican states – that make using it costly. In the long run, there is a price to pay. Nations hold one another’s currencies partly because they trust the political relationship. Mr Trump is testing what happens when they don’t. Continue reading...

data.title: Serena Williams thrills New York crowd on US Open return with Alcaraz
data.description: Former women’s No 1 proves she’s no nostalgia act before star pairing crash out in mixed doubles quarter-finals Serena Williams’ US Open return lasted two matches and one afternoon Tuesday as she and Carlos Alcaraz followed a first-round win with a quarter-final defeat by Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the headline attraction of the reimagined mixed doubles competition. Back inside Arthur Ashe Stadium 1,453 days after the defeat by Ajla Tomljanovic that had appeared to end her career, Williams emerged from the tunnel at half past three to the roars of more than 10,000 spectators. As the 44-year-old American and Alcaraz warmed up in matching purple-and-black Nike kits, public-address announcer Andy Taylor rattled off her accolades one by one to a steadily rising wall of applause. Together they carried 30 grand slam singles titles, a record for a mixed-doubles team at a major. Continue reading...

data.title: Luka Dončić looks like a superstar adrift at the Lakers
data.description: The Slovenian is one of the best players on the planet. But factors largely beyond his control have started to turn his career into a slog Luka Dončić must feel as though, these past few months, he’s been twirling in a washing machine. He announced a separation from his fiancee in March; reports followed of a prolonged custody battle over their two daughters. As Dončić plays in the NBA and his children live in Slovenia, he doesn’t see them much as is. But after the reports of the rift with his ex emerged, he started playing some of the best basketball of his life: he led the Los Angeles Lakers to a 15-2 record in March, a stretch that included a torrential 60-point display against the Miami Heat. Behind Dončić’s brightening star, the Lakers seemed to be sharpening into a real contender. Then Dončić tweaked his hamstring in April and the illusion shattered. He watched from the sidelines as the Lakers limped out of the playoffs with an inevitable second-round defeat to the Oklahoma City Thunder. Actually, Dončić must feel as if he’s been in turmoil for the past few years . He made his first – and so far only – NBA finals in 2024, leading the Dallas Mavericks there with a barrage of awesome shotmaking. As the best offensive player on the court while playing through multiple injuries, Dončić and his Mavs lost to the far deeper Boston Celtics in five games. As thanks, the Mavericks traded Dončić to the Lakers, citing defensive concerns, when what had really doomed them against the Celtics was that no one aside from Luka – who led his team in points, rebounds, assists and steals in that series – could play at the requisite level to win. Continue reading...

data.title: I once saw Enes Kanter speak truth to power. Now he only punches down | Bryan Armen Graham
data.description: Nearly a decade after I watched him defy Erdoğan at great personal cost, the ex-NBA player is using his hard-won freedom to turn transgender people into a punchline Nine years ago, I watched Enes Kanter ask America to take him in . It was May 2017, inside the National Basketball Players Association’s offices in midtown Manhattan. Kanter had just returned from a frightening detention at Bucharest airport, where Romanian border police told him Turkey had canceled his passport. He’d just turned 25, an NBA center with a green card and no country he could safely call home. “I’m open for adoption,” he joked from the head of a table in a nondescript conference room, addressing a dozen reporters hastily summoned by his manager. Then he turned serious: “My next move is to just become an American citizen.” Continue reading...

data.title: Climate-saving wonder – or €240m vanity bauble that ages like milk? The rocks set to hit Rotterdam docks
data.description: MVRDV – the firm behind Marble Arch Mound – says Rotterdam ROCKS! will inspire visitors to live sustainably. But in an era when the greenest building is the one that already exists, this tottering cairn looks set to misfire ‘It looks like something Shrek would throw up,” sniffed one online commentator, unflatteringly comparing Rotterdam ROCKS!, the recently unveiled proposal for a waterfront site in Europe’s largest port, with the vomitings of a cartoon ogre. Designed by Dutch architectural firm MVRDV, which gave London the supremely underwhelming Marble Arch Mound in 2021, Rotterdam ROCKS! (the use of EMPHATIC CAPITALS connoting an in-your-face energy) is the winner of a major architectural competition intended to create “a new world wonder”. But instead of a modern Hanging Gardens of Babylon or contemporary Colossus of Rhodes, MVRDV’s super slick renderings depict a pile of artificial “rocks” (or ROCKS!) stacked together in a humongously scaled tottering cairn, wreathed in suspiciously luxuriant foliage and sluiced by a preposterous waterfall. Continue reading...

data.title: Penny Lane Is Dead review – Aussie slasher comedy zips from Neighbours to nasty
data.description: Mia’Kate Russell’s 80s-set Ozsploitation horror is a tad slapdash, but the grungy gore and seething catfights save it from dud status Here is a muddled if energetic effort from Australian writer-director Mia’Kate Russell. There’s a little too much blurriness around the edges, making relationships and motivations slightly opaque, while the last-minute entrances and exits are a bit on the haphazard side. But as a study of seething girl-on-girl anger that leads to ultraviolence, it’s a gas. Set in Australia in 1986 (presumably because this means no mobile phones, and thus no calling for help), a trio of high-school besties prepares for a night of partying before the summer ends. Penny (Bailey Spalding) is planning to go to university to study law and asks her girlfriend Toni (Tahlee Fereday) to come with her. The two have only recently become lovers and they haven’t yet come out to their buddy Amy (Alexandra Jensen) – a sweet, childlike teen who still carries a stuffed tiger toy around for comfort. Continue reading...

data.title: ‘Why isn’t there hip-hop in 3/4 time?’: the groups reinventing a Polish folk dance for the modern age
data.description: The oberek is a traditional dance beloved of state folk ensembles – but a new generation of musicians is reconfiguring its music into wild new forms, merging folk steps with electronics and the sound of Chicago footwork It’s 6pm on the first day of OFF festival in Katowice, and a crowd is gathering in front of one of the stages to watch newcomers Tercet Imperial. Sporting disco outfits of nylon jackets, tracksuits and Chicago Bulls caps, keyboardist Piotr Zabrodzki deploys resonant acid melodies, while drummer Jan Emil Młynarski plays a rapid, irregular rhythm that brings to mind the scattergun beats of footwork, the ghetto-house subgenre that grew out of Chicago in the late 90s. Not many of those jerking their limbs to the music in front of the stage are likely to realise that they are listening to a distinctly Polish sound: that of the oberek, a traditional dance in triple metre whose name derives from the Polish verb “to spin”, because it usually accompanies couples whirling across dancefloors in a circular motion. Continue reading...

data.title: The Great Dictator by Matthew Sweet review – the fabulous life of Barbara Cartland
data.description: A brilliant new biography that does it subject the favour of taking her seriously – even if few else did Barbara Cartland was famous for dictating her novels. With a pekingese clamped to her hot pink bosom she would lie back on a library couch and exhale a story about virginal girls taming wayward dukes, damaged airmen or misunderstood surgeons. Meanwhile Miss Savory, Mrs Smith or Mrs Morgan, picked for being unfidgety and sneezeless, would take everything down in immaculate Pitman shorthand. Cartland reckoned on being able to polish off 8,000 words a day. “In this way,” she told one of the many reporters who quizzed her on her astonishing productivity, “the typescript for an 80,000-word novel is finished in a fortnight.” At her peak she was pushing out 23 books a year which added up to 723 in total. Only Agatha Christie and William Shakespeare topped her lifetime sales of 750m. Cartland was a dictator in other ways, too. Husbands, dogs, houses and the local council were all expected to bend themselves to her indomitable will. Resistance, let alone opposition, was futile. The managing director of the company that printed her books suggested that she read Nietzsche on the perceptive grounds that they had a lot of ideas in common. Oddly, he also declared himself madly in love with her. Behind that marshmallowy exterior, all pink chiffon, candyfloss hair and soft, smudgy lines, there lurked sinews of high-tensile steel. Continue reading...

data.title: Feminism for a World on Fire by Natasha Walter review – hope amid the hopelessness
data.description: A writer and activist links the climate crisis to battles for justice around the world in this vital book It has become increasingly difficult to change our minds, to question our own views or to find common ground with people we disagree with, all of which makes Natasha Walter’s new book both refreshing and exhilarating. In her ebullient 1998 debut The New Feminism, Walter hailed Margaret Thatcher as a trailblazer. In this fiercer, bleaker work, she rips into the “glossy language of aspiration feminism”, “the message that the individual woman can do anything she wants if she only has the necessary courage”. That kind of feminism inspired an “explosion of books and films about pioneers and heroines, about bossy women and gutsy girls” which retold the feminist story as “a succession of isolated campaigns, led by outsize individuals”. data.title: Triage by Claudia Rankine review – how should we respond to the world’s atrocities?
data.description: The American poet and essayist weaves memoir, fiction, criticism and lyrical lament into a tale of  friendship in an age of existential crisis “Any resemblance to actual persons, living or dead, or actual events is purely coincidental,” writes the multi-award winning Jamaican-American poet, essayist and playwright Claudia Rankine in the disclaimer to her latest work. “Unless it isn’t.” The pretzel-logic of this statement, its assertive ambiguity, sets the tone for a book that digs directly into the question of what we are to do with the idea of truth, when the world we live in is asking us “to hold, visually and emotionally, realities we do not yet have a viable system of language for”. In Triage, Rankine borrows from her personal history and from a world whose landscape now encompasses “the rise of fascism, the implementation through deportations of the Great Replacement theory, the starvation of devastated populations subjected to war and climate change”, and uses the material she gathers to pose a simple question. When faced with realities such as these, what do you do? Do you stand, or do you fall? The book begins with a friendship. Two young people – our narrator, and another she refers to only as “the theorist” – meet in college in the late 20th century, and are drawn to each other. They’re passionate; they’re idealistic; they’re committed to the activism of the time (“shantytowns were built on campus to protest apartheid South Africa”) and steeped in the texts and authors and philosophical conceits of the humanities. Over time, they develop a game. “When we spied each other during the day,” the narrator explains, “we had to collapse.” Continue reading...

In Triage, Rankine borrows from her personal history and from a world whose landscape now encompasses “the rise of fascism, the implementation through deportations of the Great Replacement theory, the starvation of devastated populations subjected to war and climate change”, and uses the material she gathers to pose a simple question. When faced with realities such as these, what do you do? Do you stand, or do you fall? The book begins with a friendship. Two young people – our narrator, and another she refers to only as “the theorist” – meet in college in the late 20th century, and are drawn to each other. They’re passionate; they’re idealistic; they’re committed to the activism of the time (“shantytowns were built on campus to protest apartheid South Africa”) and steeped in the texts and authors and philosophical conceits of the humanities. Over time, they develop a game. “When we spied each other during the day,” the narrator explains, “we had to collapse.” Continue reading...

data.title: A Pocket Full of Slagford – a retro-futurist take on Thatcher-era northern England
data.description: Developer Patrick Grant was born in Australia and lives in New Zealand, but a childhood of British TV inspired him to set a comedy game in a bleak vision of the north Something is amiss in the dingy town of Slagford, and curious scamp Pip Bunting is the only one who can find out what. So quit your mithering, it’s time to discover just how grim it truly is up north. A Pocket Full of Slagford is an upcoming retro-styled 3D puzzle adventure game set in a surreal alternative-reality near-future northern England that never escaped the clutches of Thatcherism. The story follows the misadventures of a young local lad from the eponymous Slagford after he takes ownership of a mysterious relic that lets him wreak havoc on reality. Continue reading...

data.title: The cat that fought Mussolini: how the Wulz photography sisters weaponised the family pet
data.description: Wanda and Marion Wulz defied the unbridled patriarchy of fascist Italy by shooting dancers, fencers and other famous women – as well as their cat Mucincina ‘In those fascist times,” says Federica Muzzarelli of Italy in the 1920s and 30s, “women were not free. They were regarded as mothers and homemakers. But the Wulz sisters were determined to create their own destiny. They chose photography as a way of being independent – and to show through their images that women could live that way.” Muzzarelli is the curator of Wanda and Marion Wulz: Avant-Garde Photography in 20th Century Italy, a show about to open at the Estorick Collection in London. The Wulz sisters experimented with blended and altered images more than half a century before Photoshop was invented. The most famous image to emerge from their studio was I + Cat, a self-portrait of Wanda superimposed on the face of the family pet. But the show aims to cast Marion in a new light, showing that she was no mere assistant, but rather equal to her sister in terms of photography, as they championed feminism in fascist Italy, keeping the idea of women’s emancipation alive at a time of unbridled patriarchal ideology. Continue reading...

data.title: From ‘old people music’ to owning the streets: 60 years of Notting Hill carnival and me
data.description: As a child, being taken to the Caribbean celebration was a drag. But once sound systems arrived in the 1970s, it became an unmissable yearly pilgrimage offering a sense of freedom My earliest memories of the Notting Hill carnival are of being mildly irritated. In its 1960s infancy, the event was strictly a Caribbean affair, transplanted to Ladbroke Grove as authentically as was practical. Its purpose was as obvious as its origins: giving Caribbean arrivals a chance to celebrate themselves by bringing the vibrancy of the home they left behind to these drab streets for a couple of days. Vital as this was – and it really was – it didn’t cut much ice with surly 10- or 11-year-olds like me, being dragged around behind parading steelbands. Yes, it was great to see so many Black people out in the open together and your mums and dads laughing and having a good time, but did we need to be here? There was football to be played and bikes to be ridden, yet so many of us were being forced to walk for what seemed like miles following “old people music”. Continue reading...

data.title: Russian stadium says it will not host Kanye concerts – but promoter says shows have not been cancelled
data.description: The controversial rapper now known as Ye was due to play two huge shows at St Petersburg’s Gazprom Arena, which now states it cannot host performances for contractual reasons The St Petersburg stadium that was set to host two concerts by Ye – making the rapper formerly known as Kanye West the biggest western act to play in Russia since start of the Ukraine war – has now said that the concerts will not take place at the venue, although the promoter has stressed that they have not been cancelled. Gazprom Arena had previously posted on social media saying that “the most influential musical artist of our time” would perform there on 10 and 11 October. “This is no joke!” the post stated. The event sold out immediately, including tickets priced at £1390 ($1896). Continue reading...

data.title: How I Shop with Millie Mackintosh: ‘It reminds me to get enough sleep!’
data.description: Always wondered what everyday stuff celebrities buy, where they shop for food, and the basic they scrimp on? The former reality star and author talks family heirlooms, organic veg and splurge-worthy jeans with the Filter • How I Shop with Fred Sirieix Millie Mackintosh rose to fame as part of the original cast of the reality show Made in Chelsea, filming five series before leaving in 2013. She has since established herself as a fitness, health and beauty ambassador, releasing her own beauty collection with Boots in 2017, and publishing Made: A Book of Style, Food and Fitness . After choosing to go alcohol-free, she shared her journey in the bestselling Bad Drunk , co-written with Dr Ellie Cannon. Mackintosh speaks candidly about the realities of motherhood, mental health and self-care on Instagram . Continue reading...

data.title: How to use up leftover party wine | Kitchen aide
data.description: Sauces, reductions, deglazing: our expert panel has plenty of options for making the most of undrunk vino – whether you’ve got just a capful or a whole carafe to get through What can I do with wine left over from a party? Rob, by email This is a novel concept, perhaps, but the answer essentially comes down to the quantity: “If we’re talking dribbles of red or white, that’s simple,” says Jon Atashroo, head chef/owner of Where There’s Smoke in North Yorkshire. “They go into sauces, whether that’s for pasta or to deglaze a pan before making a gravy.” Joe Otway, chef/co-owner of Higher Ground in Manchester, couldn’t agree more: “Reducing wine, be it white or red, in the base of anything is generally a good idea.” Take something tomato-based, such as ragu or chilli, as an example: “Once you’ve sweated the vegetables and there’s caramelisation on the bottom of the pan, a glass of red wine will add acidity, depth and sweetness.” And remember, you can always freeze wine dregs for later use: simply pour into ice-cube trays and stash. Moving on to medium amounts, we’re talking “stewy, fish-type things”, Atashroo says, perhaps moules marinière. Another good option is pickling: “A basic recipe is one part caster sugar, one part white-wine vinegar and one part white wine. And if you’re pickling something like beetroot, cook it in that mix, while if you’re using cucumbers, say, they go in cold.” That said, a current Atashroo go-to is altogether sweeter: “Weigh some red wine, though I don’t see why it wouldn’t work with white wine, too, add 20% of its weight in sugar, and reduce to a syrup – you’re looking for the consistency of strawberry sauce.” The result is complex and acidic, “almost like reduced port”, and great for drizzling over vanilla ice-cream. While we’re talking desserts, few things are better than fruit (peaches, figs, pears) poached in wine, either. Got a culinary dilemma? Email feast@theguardian.com Continue reading...

data.title: Country diary: A pocket rocket of rewilding – and a success in the face of opposition | Amy-Jane Beer
data.description: Asturias, Spain : I visit a farm that is thrilling in its ecological abundance, created in just eight years On a rocky 13-hectare pocket in the foothills of the Picos de Europa, Luke Massey and Katie Stacey are raising children, dogs, cattle, chicken, ducks, geese and eyebrows. In their eight years here, the farm they call Wild Finca has become a mass of scrub, with scattered large trees and dozens of clearings that Luke calls fields, but which look more like tiny irregular glades, riddled with trails and hemmed all around by the blackthorn, gorse and bramble that has sprung up around the tumbled remains of drystone walls. If Wild Finca is a forever home to the Massey-Staceys, it is a whole world to nature. Witness the butterflies and wasp spiders, the snakes, lizards, hedgehogs and sparrows, and the thousand-piece cricket orchestra that performs each evening as the glow-worms light up. It offers denning and roosting sites for foxes, pine martens, badgers and 17 species of bat, feeding opportunities for roe deer and wild boar, several species of eagle and vulture, and a pit stop for others such as the nightingale I heard singing in early morning mist. Continue reading...

data.title: Boat trips, swimming and seafood: 10 of the UK’s best harbour towns and villages
data.description: From smoked kippers in Northumberland to dolphin spotting in Dorset and a palm-fringed village on a sea loch in the Scottish Highlands The historic harbour is the hub of this working East Neuk fishing port, home to a fleet of about 30 small trawlers and creel boats. Their catches are sold at the covered market on the quay each weekday morning, and served at the harbourside Dory Bistro and Chip Ahoy at the Larachmhor pub. Pittenweem (which means “place of the cave”) also has a Victorian-era swimming pool next to the beach, which is filled by the tide twice a day. After falling into disrepair, it was saved by a local group called the West Braes Project and reopened in 2021, along with the crazy golf course. Early each August, there is an annual arts festival with exhibits by nearly 200 artists in harbourside spaces, heritage buildings, homes and studios. Pittenweem is flanked by two other pretty harbour villages, St Monans and Anstruther , while a third, Crail , is a little further north; the Fife Coastal Path links them all. The Bank in Anstruther has harbour-view rooms (doubles from £120 B&B). Continue reading...

data.title: Speeding for online glory: the internet subculture where young men drive dangerously for likes
data.description: Social media trend feeds on footage shot from cars racing down busy roads, with potentially lethal consequences The hashtags tell the story of the potentially lethal social media subculture where young men film themselves hurtling at illegal speeds down busy roads: #speedhunters, #needforspeed, #racing. The fast-driving internet trend on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube is fed by footage shot from a driver’s perspective of cars going “#fullsend” – the jargon for roaring down dual carriageways – and “#gapping” or “#swimming”, as in weaving dangerously through packed traffic. The posts attract thousands, sometimes millions of views and have been described by Andy Burnham on Monday as “truly reprehensible” . Continue reading...

data.title: Tell us: do you think AI has made Google search better or worse?
data.description: As people grow used to AI chatbots, we’d like to hear your views about Google’s search engine Google has put artificial intelligence at the front and center of its search bar. The most-visited site on the internet still shows the same list of links to users, but they have to scroll past a summarized response from an AI chatbot, a feature Google calls AI Overviews. The change to what was once the gateway to the rest of the internet has been profound, and the browsing habits of billions of people are shifting. “AI is driving the most significant upgrade of the Google Search experience ever,” Liz Reid, Google’s vice-president of search, wrote last August . In May, the company said more AI is coming . Continue reading...

data.title: Third drone and suspected military explosives found near Leipzig airport
data.description: Local media report discovery by German investigators after attempted attack on cargo and military logistics hub German investigators uncovered a third drone and suspected military explosives thought to be connected to an attempted attack on Leipzig airport, local media have reported. The drone was discovered in Kabelsketal, just to the west of the airport, along with about 50g (1.8oz) of a suspected military explosive on 14 August, 10 days after the unsuccessful sabotage . Leipzig airport is a cargo and military logistics hub used by Nato and Ukraine’s Antonov Airlines for transporting military supplies. Continue reading...

Later that day, she plans to see The Odyssey in a frigid theater. But first, there is mass. Martinez, 24, enters Our Savior Parish , the castle-like church beside her workplace, the University of Southern California. Inside, she dips her fingers in holy water, makes the sign of the cross on her forehead, and enters the main part of the church in hushed reverence. Continue reading...

data.title: Singapore sends 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes to Malaysia to recycle

data.title: In 1903, rabbits were released on Hawaii’s Laysan Island as a food source; within a decade...
data.description: German immigrant Max Schlemmer introduced rabbits to Laysan Island in 1903 for business and entertainment.  These rabbits rapidly consumed vegetation, leading to the extinction of three unique landbird species.  President Theodore Roosevelt established the Hawaiian Islands Bird Reservation to protect the remaining wildlife.  Federal authorities later removed Schlemmer and eradicated the invasive rabbit population by 1923.  Conservationists have since worked to restore the habitat and reintroduce species to the island.

data.title: O caminho da boa governança no Poder Judiciário
data.description: Em fevereiro, defendi nesta Folha que o Judiciário brasileiro precisava incorporar uma agenda de governança . Tribunais não apenas julgam: administram recursos públicos escassos, pessoas, tecnologia, infraestrutura e, sobretudo, o tempo de magistrados e servidores. Independência judicial e governança não são valores opostos. Quanto melhor governada uma instituição, maior sua capacidade de preservar legitimidade, independência e confiança social. data.title: Fiuk revela suspeita de autismo: 'Cansei de parecer o que não sou'
data.description: Fiuk, 35, afirmou nesta terça-feira (25) que suspeita ser uma pessoa dentro do espectro autista. Em um vídeo publicado nas redes sociais, o ator e cantor contou que começou a investigar a possibilidade há alguns anos. Ele interrompeu o processo por receio de ser visto de outra forma por pessoas próximas e no trabalho. "Cansei de parecer o que eu não sou. Cansei de tentar me encaixar pra fazer parte de algum grupo. Eu não sou quem eu pensava que eu fosse", disse. Leia mais (08/25/2026 - 18h43)

data.title: Do Evropy se valí nová vlna exportu z Číny. Ta hodlá i tuto příležitost využít
data.description: Odhaduje se, že se dnes v Číně vyrábí přes 70 až 80 procent všech klimatizací na světě, a to včetně produkce pro západní a japonské značky, které tam mají své továrny. Domácí trh se již nasytil, nyní přišla na řadu Evropa, která navíc chlazení potřebuje. V souvislosti s vysokými teplotami zemřelo letos pouze v Německu 14 tisíc lidí.

data.title: Sankce tvrdě dolehly na ruský diskont Mere. Prodejny v Česku zatím žijí
data.description: Ruský diskontní řetězec Mere, který má v Česku dvanáct prodejen, čelí důsledkům evropských sankcí. Finanční analytický úřad FAÚ na konci července zmrazil podíly ruským manželům Andrejovi a Anně Šnajdrovým v české provozní firmě Torgretail CZ, která českou odnož ruského řetězce zastřešuje. Obchody zatím zůstávají otevřené, v řadě evropských zemí však skončily ze dne na den.

data.title: SpaceX postaví čtvrtý kosmodrom pro Starship. Projekt má stát 100 miliard dolarů
data.description: Americká vesmírná společnost SpaceX v úterý představila projekt nového rozsáhlého kosmodromu pro své lodě Starship, který chce postavit v jižní Louisianě nejméně za 100 miliard dolarů (přes dva biliony Kč). Dohodu o zahájení výstavby čtvrtého kosmického přístavu, jež plánuje na příští rok, firma oznámila na společné akci s guvernérem Jeffem Landrym a dalšími představiteli tohoto státu na jihu USA.

data.title: Ozbrojené gangy masakrují Haiti. Desítky lidí zabily či unesly, vláda je bezmocná
data.description: Nejméně 47 lidí včetně pěti dětí v neděli zabili a přes 50 osob unesli ozbrojenci z obce Kenscoff, která leží nedaleko haitské metropole Port-au-Prince, informovala v úterý kancelář OSN na Haiti. Podle agentury AP jde o jeden ze největších únosů za poslední roky v této zemi zmítané už léta násilnostmi a politickou a ekonomickou krizí.

data.title: Velitel kurdských SDF oznámil jejich rozpuštění, začlení se do státních struktur
data.description: Velitel kurdských Syrských demokratických sil (SDF) Mazlúm Abdí v úterý oznámil jejich rozpuštění a plné začlenění do státních institucí. data.title: Opozice bránila jednání o Pavlovu vetu. Hřib ukázal Babišovu obří kreditku
data.description: Před velkým zadlužováním Česka, občanů a jejich dětí a vnoučat vládou ANO, SPD a Motoristů sobě varovala ve Sněmovně celý den opozice. Předseda Pirátů Zdeněk Hřib si k řečnickému pultíku přinesl i obří kreditku premiéra Andreje Babiše na účet občanů a varoval, že lidem vláda zadlužováním zdraží lidem hypotéky. Ministryně financí Alena Schillerová to označila jen za strašení od opozice.

data.title: „Dříve se to posílalo do plynu“. Romské studenty v Jeseníku zasypaly rasistické komentáře
data.description: Přijeli se vzdělávat a rozvíjet své schopnosti, místo toho je na internetu čekala vlna nenávisti. Romští studenti, kteří vyrazili na vzdělávací program BARUVAS v Jeseníku, se na facebookových stránkách Bruntálského a Krnovského deníku setkali se stovkami ponižujících komentářů. Některé z nich odkazovaly na plynové komory a deportace.

data.title: „Hledáme letušky starší 50 let.“ Nábor EasyJetu funguje již čtyři roky, další začíná
data.description: Jsou to už čtyři roky, kdy EasyJet spustil kampaň zaměřenou na nábor zaměstnanců starších 50 let. Od té doby se jejich počet na palubách jeho letadel více než zdvojnásobil. Většina lidí, kteří po padesátce změnili kariéru, jsou nyní podle průzkumu společnosti šťastnější. EasyJet tak boří stereotypy, že práce letušek a stevardů je pouze pro mladé.

data.title: AI drony samy určí, kdo zemře. Děsivá budoucnost je tu, Rusové nemají zábrany
data.description: Ukrajina a Rusko už otestovaly autonomní drony řízené jen umělou inteligencí. Zatímco Kyjev tvrdí, že vždy zapojuje lidský element, u Rusů se zdá, že taková omezení nemají a samostatnými bezpilotními letouny zabíjejí civilisty. Praxe přináší mnohé etické otázky, přičemž Ukrajinci varují před až dystopickými dopady.

data.title: Medvěd v kontejneru i díra v ruce od srnce. Pampalini pardubických strážníků vypráví
data.description: U městské policie v Pardubicích strávil jednatřicet let. Za tu dobu Pavel Antoch nejednou zjistil, že některé situace není radno podceňovat. Jako psovod a odchytář se setkal s tvory, které by v Pardubicích čekal jen málokdo. Někdy skončil se zraněním v nemocnici, jindy stál tváří v tvář medvědovi. Pokaždé však s odhodláním zvíře zachránit. Dnes už bývalému strážníkovi neřeknou kolegové jinak než lovec Pampalini.

data.title: Slovenská policie zmařila útok napalmem na továrnu na drony, obvinila tři cizince

data.title: Za skrýší zbraní u Berlína jsou sabotéři podporovaní Ruskem, píše magazín
data.description: V případu skrýše malého množství zbraní, kterou objevila německá policie loni nedaleko Berlína, vede stopa k sabotážní skupině organizované ruskými agenty. data.title: Britský rybář podlehl lásce k SSSR a odjel bojovat za Rusko. Přežil deset týdnů
data.description: O Nepálcích, Kubáncích či Keňanech bojujících na Donbasu toho už bylo napsáno dost a dost. Ale že by k Rusům dobrovolně narukoval Brit? Je to rarita, ale pár se jich najde. Třiatřicetiletý Bradley Townsend si nyní připsal neveselé prvenství: vstoupil do historie jako vůbec první občan Spojeného království, který padl na Ukrajině v řadách ozbrojených složek Ruské federace.

data.title: Americký řetězec se omlouvá za černošského klauna. Halloweenský kostým vzbudil emoce
data.description: Americká společnost Target se svým zákazníkům musela omluvit za dětský halloweenský kostým, který uvedla na trh. Krátce poté se na ni totiž snesla vlna kritiky za to, že produkt připomíná rasistickou karikaturu. Řetězec kostým za 25 dolarů okamžitě stáhl z prodeje. „Zmýlili jsme se a je nám to velmi líto,“ kála se firma.

Řetězec kostým za 25 dolarů okamžitě stáhl z prodeje. „Zmýlili jsme se a je nám to velmi líto,“ kála se firma.

data.title: Těhotnou partnerku ze žárlivosti napadl, teď prý žijí harmonicky. Soud k tomu přihlédl
data.description: Nezvyklý případ napadení těhotné ženy posuzoval brněnský krajský soud, před nímž stanul Michal I. Ten podle obžaloby loni v červenci zaútočil v Drahanech na Prostějovsku na svou partnerku a podle policie se tak dopustil pokusu o těžké ublížení na zdraví. S tím ovšem nesouhlasil jak muž, tak napadená, jež svého přítele od začátku hájila. A to i přesto, že po útoku skončila v nemocnici.

data.title: Zelensky congratulates Saudi Arabia’s crown prince on Makkah defense agreement
data.description:
RIYADH: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky congratulated Saudi Arabia’s Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on Monday for the recent signing of a regional defense agreement.

	Zelensky said he hopes the Makkah Joint Defense Agreement signed between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan last week will contribute to achieving security and stability in the region.

	He made the comments during a phone call with the crown prince, Saudi Press Agency reported.

	The two leaders also discussed regional and international developments.

data.title: Sports Boulevard launches $186m fund to develop Urban Wadi assets
data.description:
JEDDAH: The Sports Boulevard Real Estate Development and Investment Co. has signed agreements with Rikaz Properties to establish its third real estate investment fund, valued at more than $186 million, to develop key assets including a luxury five-star hotel in Riyadh’s Urban Wadi.

	The fund will finance the development of the hotel in the Hittin district, with Rikaz Properties serving as developer and investor and Al Jazira Capital acting as fund manager, according to an official statement.

data.description: SEOUL: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has ‌said up to 50,000 North Korean soldiers will be deployed in Russia to fight for Pyongyang’s ally, while calling on South Korea to provide support for ​its air defense.Zelensky said on X on Saturday that “a decision has been made for 30,000 to 50,000 North Koreans to be deployed on the territory of Russia,” a higher figure than his estimate of 30,000 in July. He did not elaborate on how he obtained the information.He said Kyiv had found some North Korean missiles in Ukraine’s territory, without disclosing their locations.

data.title: Iran supreme leader names Guards general Abdollahi military chief
data.description:
TEHRAN: Iranian supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei named Revolutionary Guards general Ali Abdollahi head of the country's armed forces on Monday, while also confirming a new commander of the Guards, putting his imprimatur on the country's military.
	Abdollahi had previously led the Khatam Al-Anbiya, Iran's inter-branch central military command tasked with coordinating operations.

data.title: Houthis launch new drone wave across Yemen’s government-held areas
data.description:
AL-MUKALLA: At least two Yemeni government soldiers were killed in southern Yemen as the Houthis launched a new wave of drone attacks on government-controlled areas in Aden, Mocha and Shabwa.

	The escalation came as the Yemeni army vowed on Monday to respond to Houthi drone and missile strikes on the Red Sea port city of Mocha that killed seven people and wounded 30 others.

data.title: UNESCO AI Ethics Forum highlights Saudi Arabia’s global standing, says culture minister
data.description:

data.title: Ukrainian drone attack on Russian oil hub kills 13
data.description:
Ukraine attacked the petroleum hub of Nizhnekamsk in central Russia’s Tatarstan region on Monday, killing 13 people and injuring 75 others, local authorities said, in one of the deadliest attacks in the country in the 4-year-old war.
	The Ukrainian military said it hit an oil refinery in Nizhnekamsk, which is about 1,200 kilometers (750 miles) east of the Ukrainian border and has a population of about 240,000.

data.title: Un autre incendie: le marché de Kinindo prend feu
data.description: Après les deux centres commerciaux partis en fumée ce vendredi 22 août, au centre-ville  de Bujumbura, le malheur vient encore une fois de frapper dans la matinée de ce mardi 25 août : une immense fumée s'élève au dessus du marché de Kinindo en commune Mugere au su-ouest de la capitale économique. Selon les premiers témoignages le feu est parti du côté des stands des matelas. Les sirènes des camions extincteurs s'entendent à  plusieurs kilomètres à la ronde. Ces incendies deviennent de plus en plus inquiétants et interrogent. Leur fréquence n'augure rien de bon.

data.title: Financement du budget 2026-2027 : Le président Ndayishimiye mise visiblement beaucoup sur le ministère en charge des mines
data.description: Le président burundais Evariste Ndayishimiye s’insurge contre des responsables qui s’arrogent le droit de piller les richesses de l’Etat qu’ils sont censés plutôt protéger. Le ministère en charge des mines et du commerce serait l’un de ceux qui sont mal gérés alors qu’il doit financer le budget général de l’Etat à hauteur d’au moins 50%. L’économiste Jean Ndenzako parle d’un « objectif pertinent politiquement », d’une « bonne orientation » mais qui doit s’accompagner d’une « bonne gouvernance économique » en termes de production, de traçabilité et de conformité.

data.title: Centrafrique : les députés suppléants appelés à siéger bénéficieront de toutes les indemnités liées à la fonction
data.description: Le bureau de l’Assemblée nationale s’est prononcé sur le traitement financier des députés suppléants. Désormais, lorsqu’un suppléant remplace temporairement un député titulaire empêché, notamment en raison de sa nomination au gouvernement, il doit percevoir l’intégralité des indemnités attachées à la fonction parlementaire. Cette clarification vise à mettre fin aux divergences d’interprétation concernant les droits financiers […] L’article Centrafrique : les députés suppléants appelés à siéger bénéficieront de toutes les indemnités liées à la fonction est apparu en premier sur Radio Ndeke Luka .

data.description: Les kystes ovariens sont généralement bénins et peuvent parfois ne provoquer aucun signe apparent. data.title: Bauxite de l’Adamaoua : le Cameroun pris en otage d’une guerre de capitaux
data.description: © DR Coup dur pour l'ambition minière du Cameroun. Canyon Resources abandonne son objectif de production au 4e trimestre 2026. En cause : le gel de 82 milliards FCFA (140 M$) par AFG Bank, une OPA hostile à 0,05 dollar australien sur 55,56% du capital déjà détenu, alors que le gisement de 1,1 milliard de tonnes est prêt avec 60 wagons en route. C'est un coup de théâtre dans l'Adamaoua. Alors que le pays attendait ses premières exportations de bauxite fin 2026, Canyon Resources vient de reporter sine die le projet Minim-Martap. Le couperet est tombé le lundi 24 août 2026 via un communiqué officiel. Le directeur général, Peter Secker, quittera ses fonctions d'ici fin août, signe d'une crise de gouvernance profonde. Le blocage est d'abord financier. AFG Bank Cameroun a gelé sa ligne de crédit de 82 milliards de FCFA, soit 140 millions de dollars, indispensables au démarrage. Ce gel coïncide avec une manœuvre boursière agressive. Le principal actionnaire, A2MP Investments de l'homme d'affaires Gagan Gupta, qui détient déjà 55,56% du capital, a lancé une OPA hostile pour prendre le contrôle total à prix cassé : 0,05 dollar australien l'action. Son argument : le projet ne serait plus rentable face à l'explosion des coûts logistiques. Le paradoxe est total sur le terrain. La route minière est achevée et les 60 premiers wagons commandés en Chine doivent accoster à Douala en octobre. Le gisement, l'un des plus riches au monde avec 1,1 milliard de tonnes de ressources, est prêt. Pour l'Etat, qui comptait sur Minim-Martap pour compenser le déclin pétrolier, l'attente se prolonge. Verdict le 21 septembre 2026, date de clôture de l'OPA. Cet article Bauxite de l’Adamaoua : le Cameroun pris en otage d’une guerre de capitaux est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : Léonide Mfoum quitte l’UNDP
data.description: © DR Le militant et membre de la cellule nationale de communication de l'Union nationale pour la démocratie et le progrès démissionne du parti avec effet ce 25 août 2026. Il dit refuser de continuer d'être dirigé par « des nuls ». Après 12 ans de militantisme à l’Undp, c'est terminé. Face à un parti politique « sans horizon, sans perspective », Léonide Mfoum n'a trouvé d'autre issues que de présenter sa démission. Motivée par « l'impossibilité de débat » qui règne au sein du parti et qui entrave l'examen du chemin parcouru et d'envisager des perspectives, l'homme abandonne « un malade très sérieux », rongé par « le cancer » de l'absence de débats. Aussi, le démissionnaire dénonce des dirigeants de partis « à l'épaisseur frelatée », prêts à écarter des esprits brillants pouvant leur faire concurrence. Expliquant son départ par des raisons liées à l'échec de l'Undp à la présidentielle de 2025, il pointe du doigt des dirigeants du parti qui refusent le débat, la remise en question, la réflexion ainsi que la critique. Ce qui serait à l'origine du résultat obtenu au scrutin du 12 octobre 2025. Donnant le candidat Bello Bouba Maigari 4e avec 2,45% des suffrages exprimés. « Soit une moyenne de demi sur 20 », mention « Nuls » pour les responsables du parti, d'après le militant. Il attribue cet échec au directeur de campagne en indiquant qu'il devait démissionner car n'ayant pas compris « son job ». Malgré l'échec à l'élection présidentielle, rien n'a changé à l'UNDP d'après lui. Aucune leçon n'a été tirée. « On a repris les mêmes et on est reparti ». Conclusion, pour lui, l'Undp est sous la direction des « gens qui ne voient pas plus loin que le bout de leur nez ». Par conséquent, à l'approche des élections municipales et législatives de 2027, il claque la porte sans dire qu'elle direction il va prendre. Cet article Cameroun : Léonide Mfoum quitte l’UNDP est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : trois nouvelles infrastructures à la SCDP
data.description: © DR Cette société a inauguré 3 infrastructures majeures : une sphère de gaz à Bonabéri qui augmente de 40% la capacité de stockage nationale, un nouveau pipeline Port de Douala-Bessengué et un siège social flambant neuf avec pour objectif de sécuriser l'approvisionnement en gaz et carburant. Grande annonce pour la souveraineté énergétique du Cameroun. le vendredi 21 août 2026 à Douala, la Société Camerounaise des Dépôts Pétroliers (SCDP) a inauguré trois infrastructures qui vont changer la donne. La cérémonie, présidée par le Ministre de l'Eau et de l'Énergie, Gaston Eloundou Essomba, aux côtés de la Directrice Générale de la SCDP, Véronique Manzoua épouse Moampea Mbio, a réuni autorités administratives, traditionnelles et religieuses. Le changement est concret pour les ménages. D'abord, une nouvelle sphère de gaz domestique à Bonabéri. Avec +40% de capacité de stockage supplémentaire, le Cameroun se met à l'abri des ruptures de gaz de cuisson qui pénalisent les foyers. Ensuite, un nouveau pipeline reliant le Port de Douala au dépôt de Bessengué. En accélérant le déchargement des navires pétroliers, il réduit les délais, fluidifie la chaîne logistique et diminue les tensions sur l'approvisionnement en carburant à l'intérieur du pays. Enfin, un siège social moderne, symbole de la transformation de l'entreprise publique. Pour le Ministre Eloundou Essomba, ces investissements marquent un tournant : « Nous passons d'une gestion au fil de l'eau à une approche fondée sur l'anticipation, la résilience et la souveraineté énergétique. » Un signal fort pour sécuriser le quotidien des Camerounais. Cet article Cameroun : trois nouvelles infrastructures à la SCDP est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Souveraineté agricole : le CENEEMA livre la ferme semencière de Ngouang
data.description: © DR 123 hectares aménagés sur 100 prévus, pour 400 millions de FCFA financés par le PIISAH : le CENEEMA a rempli son cahier de charges sur la ferme semencière de Ngouang. Un projet pour produire des semences hybrides de maïs et soja et réduire les importations. Le Centre National d'Etudes et d'Expérimentation du Machinisme Agricole (CENEEMA) vient de matérialiser une ambition du gouvernement : faire de Ngouang une vitrine technologique au service des producteurs. Situé dans la commune de Yoko, département du Mbam-et-Kim, région du Centre, le site a été visité le mardi 18 août 2026 par la Directrice Générale, Andrée Caroline Mebande Bate, accompagnée du MINADER, des élites locales et des autorités traditionnelles. Porté par l'entreprise RBH GROUP Sarl et financé par le MINADER via le Programme d'Import-Substitution Agropastoral et Halieutique (PIISAH), le projet a vu le CENEEMA déployer tout son Pool de Mécanisation de Yoko : bulldozers pour le défrichement, tracteurs, charrues, semoirs pneumatiques de précision et pulvérisateurs à rampes de 2000 litres. Objectif double : produire des semences hybrides de maïs et de soja adaptées aux zones agro-écologiques, et démontrer l'impact de la mécanisation sur les rendements. La ferme est conçue comme un pôle intégré qui rapprochera les intrants de qualité des bassins du corridor Ntui-Yoko-Lena-Tibati-Meiganga. Les travaux ont été réceptionnés par la commission technique conjointe MINADER-MINMAP-CENEEMA. Au-delà de l'infrastructure, le projet génère déjà des emplois directs et indirects et stimule le transport et le commerce local. Pour le CENEEMA, bras séculier de l'Etat en mécanisation, c'est une pierre essentielle pour l'autosuffisance alimentaire prônée par la SND30. Cet article Souveraineté agricole : le CENEEMA livre la ferme semencière de Ngouang est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: COP17 : le Cameroun plaide son projet Sahel vert
data.description: © DR Conduite par le ministre HELE Pierre, la délégation camerounaise participe à la COP17 sur la désertification en Mongolie. Au programme : négociations sur l'eau, migration et sécurité, et une rencontre avec les Emirats Arabes Unis pour le financement de Kaélé. Le Cameroun fait entendre sa voix contre la désertification. Depuis le 17 août 2026 à Oulan-Bator, la capitale de la Mongolie, accueille la 17e Conférence des Parties à la Convention des Nations Unies pour la lutte contre la désertification, sous le thème "Restaurer les terres, Restaurer l'espoir". La délégation camerounaise est conduite par le Ministre de l'Environnement, HELE Pierre, accompagné du Secrétaire Général du MINEPDED, le Pr Paul Tchawa, et du Point Focal de la Convention, David Payang. Depuis le 24 août dernier après l'ouverture du segment de haut niveau par le Premier ministre mongol Nyam-Osoryn Uchral, le Ministre HELE Pierre a présidé le segment ministériel sur les liens entre dégradation des terres, sécheresse, mobilité et sécurité, avant un dîner officiel offert par le chef du gouvernement mongol. L'agenda s'annonce chargé. Ce 25 août 2026, le Cameroun interviendra sur la journée dédiée à l'Eau, avec au centre des débats la rétention d'eau dans les paysages, la restauration des sols et la lutte contre l'érosion. Point d'orgue le 27 août avec trois rendez-vous clés : une table-ronde de l'OIM sur Migration et Sécurité, une seconde sur le financement de la prise en compte des migrations dans les plans de développement, et surtout une bilatérale Cameroun - Emirats Arabes Unis. A l'ordre du jour : le partage de l'expérience camerounaise du Sahel Vert et les opportunités de financement du complexe agro-industriel de Kaélé. Une COP cruciale alors que 40 à 75% des terres mondiales sont dégradées. Cet article COP17 : le Cameroun plaide son projet Sahel vert est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

Ce 25 août 2026, le Cameroun interviendra sur la journée dédiée à l'Eau, avec au centre des débats la rétention d'eau dans les paysages, la restauration des sols et la lutte contre l'érosion. Point d'orgue le 27 août avec trois rendez-vous clés : une table-ronde de l'OIM sur Migration et Sécurité, une seconde sur le financement de la prise en compte des migrations dans les plans de développement, et surtout une bilatérale Cameroun - Emirats Arabes Unis. A l'ordre du jour : le partage de l'expérience camerounaise du Sahel Vert et les opportunités de financement du complexe agro-industriel de Kaélé. Une COP cruciale alors que 40 à 75% des terres mondiales sont dégradées. Cet article COP17 : le Cameroun plaide son projet Sahel vert est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : admission en licence professionnelle, le Minesup durcit le ton contre les IPES
data.description: © DR Un rappel à l'ordre du ministre d'État, ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur, Jacques Fame Ndongo, interdit l'accès à la licence aux profils dépourvus du niveau Bac+2, sonnant la fin des pratiques contraires dans des instituts privés d'enseignement supérieur. La question ne devrait pas se poser. Un étudiant obtient une licence au bout de six semestres d'études correspondants aux trois années de licence. La sortie du ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur rappelle la norme du système LMD appliqué dans l'enseignement supérieur au Cameroun. La licence professionnelle est ouverte aux candidats titulaires d'un diplôme national sanctionnant deux années d'enseignement supérieur valides. Elle est réservée aux titulaires d'un Diplôme d'études universitaires générales (DEUG), d'un Brevet de technicien supérieur (BTS), d'un Higher National Diploma (HND), d’un Diplôme universitaire de technologie (DUT) ou d'un titre équivalent, rappelle le ministre dans une communication en date du 21 août 2026 et rappelant à l'ordre certains IPES. Pour avoir sa licence professionnelle, le candidat doit ajouter deux semestres d'études ou de formation sur son diplôme initial de niveau BAC+2. Si le Minesup insiste sur cette décision, c'est en raison du fait que des établissements privés d'enseignement supérieur recrutent des candidats avec le BAC pour les former en une année. Et leur délivrer le diplôme de licence. Pourtant, les détenteurs du BAC sont admissibles à une inscription au niveau supérieur en vue d'obtenir un DEUG, un BTS, ou un HND. Le ministre rappelle à ce sujet que l'accès aux formations aboutissant aux examens nationaux de BTS ou du HND est conditionné par le Baccalauréat, le GCE Advanced Level ou d'un diplôme équivalent. À quelques semaines de la rentrée académique pour le compte de l'année 2026/2027, le ministre de l'Enseignement supérieur interpelle les promoteurs des IPES à l'effet de « respecter strictement cette mesure réglementaire » sous peine de de sanctions. La mise en garde du Minesup se présente aussi comme une mesure visant à sauvegarder la qualité de la formation, à préserver le niveau des étudiants formés, à assurer leur compétitivité sur le terrain. Il y va aussi de la crédibilité du système éducatif camerounais au moment où des voix s'élèvent pour dénoncer la baisse du niveau scolaire d'une part et encourager le renforcement de la professionnalisation des enseignements d’autre part. Cet article Cameroun : admission en licence professionnelle, le Minesup durcit le ton contre les IPES est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

data.title: Cameroun : le Minesec ouvre le paiement électronique des inscriptions, frais d’examens et concours
data.description: © DR Le ministre des enseignements secondaires, Pauline Nalova Lyonga, vient d'indiquer les modalités de paiement des contributions exigibles et des frais d'examens officiels pour le compte de l'année scolaire 2026/2027. Les parents, tuteurs et élèves peuvent s'acquitter des contributions exigibles ainsi que des frais d'inscriptions des candidats aux examens et concours pour l'année scolaire 2026/2027 à compter du 24 août 2026. Les paiements peuvent se faire en ligne en suivant une procédure indiquée mettant au centre des opérations le matricule de l'élève. Elle est contenue dans une communication du ministre en date du 24 août qui en présente les repères essentiels. D'après les points clés listés à respecter cette année, l'obtention du matricule sur la plateforme cartescolaire.cm ou auprès des établissements scolaires est l'étape préliminaire. Pour ce qui est des matricules des élèves des classes de sixième, Form one et première année, ils doivent être générés sur la plateforme par leurs établissements scolaires respectifs. Par ailleurs, les chefs d'établissements scolaires publics et privés ont le devoir d'effectuer leur conseil de classe de fin d'année scolaire 2025/2026 sur la plateforme cartescolaire.cm . Dans sa communication, le ministre indique aussi la démarche à suivre pour les élèves transférés d'un établissement scolaire à un autre. Ces derniers vont s'assurer que leur matricule est dans le nouvel établissement avant de procéder à un quelconque paiement. Aussi, à la différence des autres versements qui se font avec le matricule unique, les frais du concours d'entrée en sixième, aux École normales des instituteurs d'enseignement général et aux Écoles normales des instituteurs d'enseignement technique doivent être payés en utilisant le code de l'établissement sur la plateforme cartescolaire.cm . La plateforme créée pour centraliser le fichier national des établissements scolaires et des élèves permet aussi de sécuriser les transactions et d'éviter des désagréments souvent causés par des responsables de mauvaise foi. Pour désengorger les intendances des établissements scolaires, les paiements électroniques se font auprès des opérateurs Campost, Express Union, MTN Cameroon et Afriland First Bank. L'ouverture des opérations de paiement le 24 août annonce l'entrée effective dans la dernière ligne droite conduisant à la fin des vacances et au début de l'année scolaire suivant le calendrier de l’année scolaire 2026-2027 rendu public il y a quelque temps. Cet article Cameroun : le Minesec ouvre le paiement électronique des inscriptions, frais d’examens et concours est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .
